name: Tom Leonard
subject: Feb. 27th - Positive Path Newsletter
body:
[](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/C3V892aNF763m2suuin4fWbMgg/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg)
---
Dear Friend,

February is almost done!

Time goes fast when you're busy on the campaign trail!

Here are some highlights from this past week:

• Our campaign team traveled to data center meetings in Van Buren Township, Lowell, Dorr, and Livingston County throughout the week

• On Thursday I spoke at the Livingston County GOP

• On Friday we had a meeting with our Next-Gen Coalition to catch up and hear their input on the race so far and what we can do to continue improving our campaign!

• We launched our TikTok Account! Give us a follow! [You can check that out here.](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/PNB8QZhvxGDZLNSJUHboQA/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg)
---
Let's make this week even better!
Together, we are creating The Path Forward.
**Keeping Education Dollars with Michigan Students**
A few weeks ago, during my time in the Upper Peninsula, I shared a press release to my social media pages about the School Aid Fund.
[You can check it out here.](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/ALbo763erh7Sd892o0XA37XhdA/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg)

This release highlights an important issue of our campaign - fixing our education system. There is no reason why our state should be taking $1.7B from the School Aid Fund and giving it to universities. We need to prioritize Michigan students in K-12.

Our focus is on Michigan students, and putting power back in the hands of parents.
There's no budging on that.

Read more about this and the rest of the newest edition of 'The Path Forward' at www.tomformichigan.com
---
**Next-Gen Spotlight**
Our Next-Gen Spotlight for this week is Nick Slager from Central Michigan University.
"I support Tom Leonard because he cares more about the mental health crisis in our nation more than any other person running for any office in the country."
-Nick Slager

---
Thank you, Nick, for all you do to help our campaign! Our Next-Gen Coalition is paving the way for Michigan's future!
**Join the Team!**

It's with your help that results come. We would love to have you join the team!

• Volunteer Today: Sign up for phone banking, door-knocking, events, or hosting a meet-and-greet in your community. Your time makes all the difference! [Sign Up Here](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/4OvIztKfEerWzTRRv2su1A/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg) and reach out to our Field Director, Tony, for more volunteer opportunities at tony@tomformichigan.com

• Continue sharing our positive vision on social media - follow my X account's, [@Tom4Michigan](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/nbllKzCDfwvIbopuJ2E0vA/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg) and [@TomLeonard28](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/GbMNopSXwePXyWOLpmWnvg/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg), my [Facebook page](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/cAnopwOcAe763kXeY763wkY3NQ/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg), and my [Instagram](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/LxCxPqa892YtUAC3vBhFqcKA/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg)
Thank you for the constant support of our vision.

Let's keep the momentum going and make this week another great one!

God bless you and your loved ones. Have a great week.

Best,

**Tom Leonard**
Candidate for Governor
---

To learn more, get involved, and donate visit [www.TomForMichigan.com](https://sendy.right-strategies.us/l/cve9YluPeAoOO3uAO6KV4g/XhcJVCC763rjLWURDWL9Fl3g/D7YrLG4Up3aCZSeKzJgzHg)

subject: the shortest month
body:
|

# A night of music, community, and a little hope.

Hey Peter,I'll be honest: sometimes you just need a night out with good people.That's exactly why I'm excited to invite you to join us on **Friday, March 13th,** at the **45th Parallel Distillery in New Richmond** from **5:00 to 9:00 pm** for an evening of live music, great food, and the kind of conversations that remind you why any of this matters.We're welcoming **Nashville recording artist Trey Taylor** for what I know will be a special night. Trey has a gift for telling stories that feel like your own. The struggles, the hopes, the sense that things can and should be better for everyday people. His music hits different when you're surrounded by neighbors who get it.**Table 65** is handling the appetizers (trust me, you'll want to come hungry), and we'll have plenty of time for laughter, honest talk, and maybe a little dancing.This district can be flipped. I truly believe that. But it starts with moments like this. People showing up, connecting, and deciding together that fairness and decency are worth fighting for.**Come be part of it.** Click below to secure your seat. _(The page also has instructions if you'd prefer to pay by check!)_

Dear Friend, Something new launches on March 1, and it is long overdue.For years, the Swamp has relied on friendly media, closed door deals, and selective coverage to control the narrative. That ends now.We are officially launching **Freedom Caucus Unfiltered** , a new weekly radio show and podcast that will bring you the Freedom Caucus perspective on national and state politics. The first episode airs **March 1 at 7pm CT / 8pm ET** on NewsTalkSTL 101.9 FM in St. Louis.The hosts are seasoned radio voices Tim Jones, our Missouri State Director, and Missouri State Senator Nick Schroer - the chairman of your **Missouri Freedom Caucus**. Both are experienced broadcasters who understand how to break down complicated political fights and expose what is really happening behind the scenes.Our first guest sets the tone.Mark Meadows will join the inaugural episode. He is a former Chief of Staff to President Trump and one of the founding members of the **House Freedom Caucus**. Eleven years after the House Freedom Caucus launched, the state movement it inspired is now active in 15 states and growing. The purpose of **Freedom Caucus Unfiltered** is simple. We will share the stories unfolding daily across our 15 states, highlight the good work of the House Freedom Caucus in Washington, and provide a direct channel for truth without media filters.You can listen live on March 1. We’re joining Make the Road Action Pennsylvania, Lehigh Valley DSA, and Lehigh County Executive Josh Siegel in supporting Ce-Ce ahead of the May 19th primary because HD-22 deserves a bold, proven champion for working people.
**Ce-Ce has already shown what that leadership looks like, Peter.**
As the _top_ vote-getter in her 2023 re-election to Allentown City Council, she has earned deep trust in the community. She led the charge to pass Allentown’s “Welcoming City” policy to protect immigrant families from unjust enforcement. She has fought for renters, stood up for workers, and supported small businesses trying to survive in a tough economy. She doesn’t just talk about working-class power — she organizes alongside people to build it.
**Now she’s stepping up to take that fight to Harrisburg and deliver for families across the Lehigh.**
Her opponent was selected by party insiders in a closed-door process and has never faced a competitive primary. But at WFP, we believe democracy belongs to the people, not political gatekeepers.
Winning this race won’t be easy. The establishment will have its corporate donor network, but we have something stronger: a grassroots movement powered by teachers, service workers, caregivers, immigrants, young people, and long-time residents who want a government that reflects and fights for them.
**If we’re going to elect Ce-Ce and continue building governing power for working people in cities like Allentown — city by city, block by block — we need to invest early and organize now.**

The establishment will have its corporate donor network, but we have something stronger: a grassroots movement powered by teachers, service workers, caregivers, immigrants, young people, and long-time residents who want a government that reflects and fights for them. If we’re going to elect Ce-Ce and continue building governing power for working people in cities like Allentown — city by city, block by block — we need to invest early and organize now. Every dollar helps us organize, knock doors, make calls, and turn out the voters who believe in a government that works for working families, not corporations and insiders. The PA Working Families Party has been organizing and winning in Allentown and across the Lehigh Valley for years. This endorsement is about more than one race. It’s about building durable power for working people and sending leaders to Harrisburg who are accountable to our communities. Let’s win this together. subject: We need to talk about Trump.

body:

Hi, friend, Deb Haaland here.

We need to talk about President Trump's lies, half-truths, and exaggerations.

When President Trump talks about lifting millions of people off of food stamps, what he is really saying is that _he has kicked millions of people off of food stamps._
When he talks about our country and our streets being safer because he is addressing immigration, that is an outright lie. _In reality, people are living in fear across our country, and he is ripping families apart, including right here in New Mexico._
When he talks about lowering costs, that is a complete exaggeration. _In reality, things are more expensive._ I know this firsthand. When I shop, what used to cost me $20 now costs me $50.
Friend, it's never been more clear: President Trump is not delivering for working families. He's attacking our communities, dismantling our healthcare, and handing out tax breaks to billionaires. **Enough is enough.**
That’s why I am not afraid to stand up to Donald Trump or anyone in his administration. I have been a brick wall to Trump in Congress, and I promise to be a brick wall to Trump as governor of New Mexico.
The GOP knows that governors are the last line of defense when the federal government, including President Trump, abuses its power. They also know electing a Republican governor this November is their only hope to bring their extremist agenda here — they know I won’t stand for it. That's why they're throwing money at this race to flip New Mexico red.
We can't let that happen. Now more than ever, we need to show the GOP that we have a strong grassroots movement powering our campaign: **[Please, will you rush $5, or whatever you can spare, to help me reach my end-of-month fundraising goal, win in November, and continue to act as a brick wall against Trump?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5778?t=1&akid=7837%2E400544%2Eke3RB9)**
Be Fierce,
Deb

Friends , I want to share a bit about my personal life that you may not know yet.
I was raised by social justice warriors.
My dad marched for civil rights in Selma, Alabama, where he heard Martin Luther King Jr. preach. My mom, born and raised in the Philippines, spent years fighting for the restoration of democracy in her home country.
My parents had me while living and working in the Philippines as social justice missionaries. I was born when a dictator was rising to power and martial law was imminent.
It was critical to both of my parents that I grow up in a country with democracy, freedom, rule of law, and human and civil rights — and sadly it became clear to them that wasn’t the case in the Philippines. So they brought my family here, to California, when I was just two months old.
A short while later, my parents began working with the United Farm Workers of America — fighting for workers’ rights, fair pay, and shade and water breaks alongside Dolores Huerta, Cesar Chavez, and Philip Vera Cruz.
I would never have guessed as a young kid that I would grow up to serve as the Attorney General of California — but as long as I can remember, I’ve known that I wanted to fight for those most vulnerable to have a fair shot at the California Dream.
That’s why I do this work. I know, without a doubt, that the California Dream is alive and well because I’m living mine — and I’m committed to using every bit of platform and power I have to lift people up and fight for justice for all.
I’m up for re-election in November, and I want nothing more than to continue this fight.
California needs an Attorney General who will stand up to those who abuse their power — whether it’s corrupt politicians, corporate polluters, extremist groups trying to roll back our rights, or powerful interests that exploit workers, cheat consumers, and put profits ahead of people.
So I’m asking you for help: Will you donate to my re-election campaign before our February deadline tomorrow night? Every single dollar we raise right now helps us build a stronger grassroots movement to protect our freedoms — and win in November. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]

Thanks very much for your support. It means a lot to me to have you on this team.
-Rob

name: Eileen for Colorado
subject: Former Congressman Ed Perlmutter Endorses Retired Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher
body:
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE****Date:** February 26, 2026 **Contact:**[ Taylor Gillespie](mailto:taylorg@eileenforcolorado.com), 720-557-6185
---
| | **Former Congressman Ed Perlmutter Endorses Retired Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher**
_Perlmutter Backs Laubacher as the Only Democrat Positioned to Win_
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **Highlands Ranch, CO** – Today, retired Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher announced the endorsement of former U.S. Congressman Ed Perlmutter, a widely respected Colorado leader known for his integrity, bipartisan work ethic, and relentless focus on delivering results for the people he served. During his eight terms in Congress, Perlmutter earned a reputation for championing working families, protecting small businesses, expanding veterans’ benefits, and helping communities cut through federal red tape. His endorsement signals strong confidence in Laubacher’s ability to bring principled, solutions-focused leadership to Washington at a moment when Congress needs it most.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | _“Eileen Laubacher has exactly what it takes to win in Colorado’s 4th District. She’s the kind of candidate that Republicans, Democrats, and independents can all get behind because Eileen listens, she leads, and she’s committed to doing what’s best for the people who call this district home,”_ **said former Congressman Ed Perlmutter.** _“She is the real deal, and she’s the leader rural Colorado deserves in Congress.”_ _“I’m honored to have Congressman Perlmutter’s support,”_ **said retired Rear Admiral Eileen Laubacher.** _“Ed spent his career doing exactly what public service is supposed to look like - showing up, listening, solving problems, and fighting like hell for the communities he represented. That’s the standard Colorado deserves. Whether it’s protecting our land and water, defending our veterans, standing up for our farmers and ranchers, or helping families keep up with rising costs, we need leaders who will put people above partisanship. That’s what I’ve done my entire life, and that’s what I’ll do in Congress.”_ Eileen, the daughter and granddaughter of Navy veterans, began her military service at the U.S. Naval Academy under President Reagan and rose to the rank of Rear Admiral as an intelligence officer. She deployed to Afghanistan while raising five children and spent more than three decades leading sailors, advising senior national security officials, and defending the Constitution she swore an oath to protect._Titles, ranks, and military service are used for identification purposes only and do not imply endorsement by the Department of Defense.__**##**_

We can only do this with your help.
Heidi started this grassroots campaign for Congress in Grass Valley almost an entire year ago because she was tired of waiting for change.
Our district deserves a leader who understands what we're going through every day and actually cares about moving past the toxic politics in Washington to deliver results.
And half measures aren't results.
For far too long politicians have worked with their corporate donors to push for moderate policies that uphold the status quo.
Heidi is running to be the change that we desperately need, and she's ready to fight tooth and nail to stop this administration, push for Medicare for All and a Green New Deal, and stand up for working families.
But because she isn't taking a single cent from corporate PACs, we need your help.
Friend, it's going to take people power to counter the hundreds of thousands of dollars that our opponents have received from corporate PACs and groups like AIPAC, and we can only do it with your support.

Raised by parents who had persisted to make a middle-class life for their kids in Contra Costa County while lifting up others, Heidi was taught to push through and overcome challenges rather than complain about them. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.
After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.
Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

Clinton Under Oath Today

Former President Bill Clinton testified under oath Friday to the House Oversight Committee as part of its [probe into Jeffrey Epstein](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGypCAQRb9GMyxsGdGAYBOz2XRDC7GVrkWwgNF5f_-KqfcFL7tB9617zr_n_NTkyO9_9YHKXDSvYZ0Xcs448jn4lF_RB58t2pDTDBx6xoGBnL2b23pVZu07qFG1UgLAOEhRWyU708t2GOUgRCs33vHHOBr-AG3EBog1qdLEASQAF13bQLcN0BqhF9PxhxSV4K9z1RlTY4JPGC-d6ULyPpQUfGPCUTtlcz5T1f2pYKpguu-72cLb413ejgqmMzjKZFIFU6FiP1hs0wYTs7RblrL-X3J4JWR7JFd8MDxTRvLsjGFBpreMkVlyTscvtjidcmIbJfs5fZ-4UhlVR7Wed2lIvawE3w9N7rM0_0LupeA7AAD__xkZjhE) -- the first time a former president has been compelled to testify before Congress in over 40 years. Clinton told lawmakers in his opening statement that he "saw nothing" and "did nothing wrong." The deposition follows wife Hillary's defiant six-hour session Thursday, during which she [deferred at least a dozen questions](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOhCAURb8GOww8ULSg2MZutt3SIOD4EnwYYZz9_I2b7A9sd5p7T-79eswPhwnp-en2aP2Fc8hhXjAln5BqplJfJ2WqW9xyLTMI6LkADmamNMsmWB96BU200hgAGAejm81qp2JUqxxXOQTwneu7ceycWmEwy7rIBu3dJAAMgNBKtqDWAaTXbvFKdEYzLV5HcDWW1mcq8bxcxSsiUb4pU-vz3iS71XoUpj4YTAym0wXM7Zq_Kb7v4M5gukUMJgE3GwbT3zL-zPxFIZ48u7pxJB6PUiMSP868RAZTc9pwvDElLL1hWjx3h-lXXP_x1WXhJwAA__9q4Hhe) to her husband. Chairman James Comer (R-KY) says the committee's questions will cover Clinton's flights on Epstein's jet, photos with Epstein and Maxwell, and events Epstein attended at the Clinton White House. Democrats responded by [demanding Trump also testify](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOhCAQQL8GOjY4oGBBcY3dXnulURjXuSAYYd3c31_c3Bdc95JJ5s2br_t4nyhSenxOGzp_0hhyGGeK0UdKNadSn0fKqa645lpGkNAJCQLMmOLY8OB86BRwdI0xANBbo_nq-k5Z4xVIVEa10li99MrgAtbbebaBk7s2SQADILVqbqAWC43X0-yVbI1mWj73MFUsN59TweOcKp1IKeWLcrr5vPHo1lr3wtQHg4HBcJ1JMV4zBsOaN0z4Km98FmQwtKa1vQZxFYq_RPGNy3Lgj8C9VKQkAu650CVhMPDDhf1FMVLpDNPysU30FvD6j3-dDn4DAAD__2HQer8) -- a transparent deflection from the Clintons' mounting credibility crisis. ★★★
Embassy Evacuation Signals Iran

The State Department authorized non-essential embassy personnel and families to leave Israel on Friday as the threat of [U.S. strikes on Iran](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOnTAQRb8GOj-ZgcX7Coo0r9u0KdGAh2USM0aeAZJ8fUQ-YburK52rq_PjY_xATiyf33GjYT55jDmOE6c0JxbLonYUyWIrrdl0BA-98-AgjJLGpo7DHPsWahqaEADg-R66eh0iwbMJU4_P0C9IGMmHuCxL7N-6-CRf83AveYAA4Lu2eUC7vEMzdzjNrX8LXdX5Y49opI85i1I50fgkFsl3yvKY81anYTXbtWq_VfCq4HVd12PJv4WuG9vuJpcUK3ipoZGLtJvDw9Zc-C-pkyyOVEmMMblDHW0Tqv5xOxXNIpTcTyqHYqLthrGYw5Uwuj2r8pTIcUFxaoV_kdZliPvFKbH2oer854ac_h-1L7g9B_gXAAD__9uHj64) grows closer by the hour. Ambassador Mike Huckabee emailed staff to leave "TODAY," warning that commercial flights could become scarce. The move comes after CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper [briefed President Trump](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOrSAQQL8GOw2OKFhQvIbuvnZLMwL3SnaEG0Hd_fsN-wnbncxMTk7m47E8MFCIr_-4e22vsLjkljUQWQqxpJjLecQUy-a3VPICHKaWQwtyibT0jdPWTQM0XvdSAsCspGg2PTsxjwrkbL3jo4Bx8nLgakW3WuUn1QRdTRxAAnAx9B0MTwW9FbjagY9SMMHPt8Pic2dTzP64sITLhxhTpRQ7m_aG9FbKO7PhHwPDwNz33UV_5x2_6r5O0kGOgXlRWpEK0icDEw6M7ZnbkA_01Pp9xZy_21zw-WRgahoDw6GyrPfV0IOQU68YmObQ7n0HopAnyQR_7Rjot6f84YWXhp8AAAD__wTWfh0) on military options Thursday -- the first such briefing since the Iran crisis began in December. Vice President Vance told Fox News there is "no chance" of a prolonged war, adding that Iran should [take Washington's threats seriously](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0LFuwyAUheGnwVssOLhce2Do4i1dO1oEcHwlDFEgdh-_Sh-h21nON_zf1-XqOHG-f7k9Wn_wEkpYbpyST5xbybW9nrnktsWttLpAwlwkLqAlp0V1wfpgNLpoFRGAaaSh26yZ9DRSiPCk4FdIkmbFqkY4ouh8x_YtSYAAOWjVQ68jlB_czWv5QYMY5OsRXIu19yXX-Dxc4yNyzuW9Su592btkt9YeVehPgVlgPs-zX8tPjuf7tgvMB4dYBGajJylp0kYrhe5pw-PklLgaEoO8747TH9j-0eCw-A0AAP__Ujtpog). Nuclear talks in Geneva ended Thursday with no breakthrough, and Iran's armed forces warned that any American action "will lead to a widespread fire in the region." ★★★
DOJ Sues Five More States

The Department of Justice sued five additional states Thursday -- Utah, Oklahoma, Kentucky, West Virginia, and New Jersey -- for refusing to hand over [voter registration records](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2OpDAQhJ_GZEamzeCZwMElZHPphcg_zeCTaSPcwD7-in2EzSoo1af6_r2nt0s50eevW9GGM02xxMmnnENOxIUqHzsV4gWXwnUCBYNUIMFMlKeuiTbEQUODtjMGAF5P0zeL7TAGeGgzm9fsvDL-pWN0s_ed93HQjybZe0kBGADV664FPT-hC73zQauH6UWvji06xtqGQhX303E6MRGVOxVqQ1mbbBfmrQr9R8AoYLyuq83pRCrXXL7uioCR8KoCxv9H5RRQRtzczisSy3pglWvZUVa-UfIsjLuMjp28P0oYWrduzW7jdqWcUx2M6NVndSn_8PkXyk4L3wEAAP___Nt9_g), bringing the total to 29 states and Washington, D.C. AG Pam Bondi called accurate voter rolls "a requisite for the election integrity that the American people deserve." Notably, four of the five states voted for Trump in 2024, proving this isn't partisan -- it's about [clean elections everywhere](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLHSnSAQRp8GOxxcuRf_giKN3Z82pYOw6mYQHFg1j5_x5g3SbbFzvjPn1_f07ShSWn-6Ha2_aAo5TDPF6CMlzqnyWVJOvOGWuU6g4C0VSDBTilPXBOvDu4cGbWcMAHwNRjebxc6_lAOHiLAsKnzN5qWdmT1gZ2Y_NGQfkgIwAEr3XQv9MkDntZt9r15GC63OIzjG2vqcKpbLMV1IKeXnyqn1eW-i3ZiPKvofAkYB433f7e3qRmnlnPCP2ylheV4FjAnvKmDU2mg19ALGkH_LemKVC10oKz9rcslFLv-aSM7yKDmcHuVyxiivzFhkwZUql4-FjFT5oTbFhuOmGKm-jdBq3R3FjyP_R9bLwt8AAAD__48tizg). AAG Harmeet Dhillon said officials who refuse to be transparent are "choosing to fight us in court" rather than show their work. The push comes as Congress debates the [SAVE America Act](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckD1uhDAQhU8DnVf2wMJu4SIN3aZNiYw9wERmjOyBvX5ElBOke8X3fvS-XuPLUSRePt2G1p80hhTGiWL0kVgSFzkyJ5YV1yRlBA2d0qCgHzmOpg7Wh66BGq3pewB4Pvq2Xm1jZjNrgxrvvtVGOz01j27S7omTMfNUk72SNEAPoNvG3KCZH2B86ybf6HvfVq0-9uAEy80nLphPJ3QiMadLJb75tNXRriJ7qZqPCoYKhu-jiKzI-L5sWwXDkk7MvCFLBYNPR5aionv_seRRBdxdlotQ5cCiZjpRFbmqlfMeS1FnEswqpxiLIvbxCMSLmtORVcZQZxv2N8VIpeurVi-bo_g7T_7x6GnhJwAA___-loqf) requiring proof of citizenship to vote in federal elections.

Harris Teases 2028 Again

Karl Rove warned Friday that Kamala Harris and Gavin Newsom are running a ["shadow primary"](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0DGO6yAUheHVQBfrciFgFxSvcZfXTokI4PhKGCJD7Fn-yLOE6U5zvuL_eriHp0zl9d9vyYaDXKzRPSnnkKn0Wlr_7KWWvqa19uYQUN8Ab2hcyU7waEPUEnmywhhEnEaj-GqXu5iifqoQRyNBh7vWEwY_qlFKuSTgZC8JEA0iKCkGlMuIIij_DBLuRjEFn3f0PbUh1NLSfvhOR6JS6rVqGULdeLZr7-_G5D-GM8P5PM9hqd8lnddtYzgfFFNlOGs5ARgQ0giBfLfxfVLO1LRhCl6bp_wL9j80OCz-BAAA__8wlGls) for 2028, with Harris confirming this week she's "thinking about it." Good luck with that.

★★★
Dems Grilled on SOTU Refusal

Democrats are facing heat for refusing to stand when Trump said the government's first duty is to protect American citizens — a moment Fox News called the [most viral clip](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0LHOpCAUBeCnwQ6DF0a0oNjGbrbd0lyBGW-CFyOMZt5-4_8If_clJzknOf-e8xMpEb__4hadP2kOOcwLpeQTcc1c6ufgzHWNa65lBgW9VCDBzpzmrgnOh15DE11nLQCMgzXN6hZt-hEe_gUP2weMaPrFBK8GRIUDxobc3aQALIAyumtBvwbovMHFa_WwRhj12QPWWFqfucTjxEpnJOZ8K3Pr89Ykt9a6F6H_CJgETNd1tV9cc75TARPHqwiY8KjkU7x5IvsoC36LxC0e5FF6ZM5V7vmKh-xGbQ2Mo27XuqXmcGG_KCUqvRVGvTek9LNcf3HW6eB_AAAA__8ABXpO) of the entire address.

A coalition of conservative state watchdogs released a report showing they identified [$28 billion in waste and fraud](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0LGyozAMBdCvgc4ZEH5xUrjYJt3bdkvGyCJ41kge2-D3-TvkE7ZTozP33j_f87cLMfD7t9vJ4hlmL35eQowYA1fhUo_MwnWjTWqZYYC7GkCBmTnOY-8t-vsEPdnRGAB4PozuN-vpy9Bzei4LLSMs_oEe9YRP0Mbfp3Hog72kAcAADHoabzCtDxhRuwWn4cvoTg9H8q5SuaFwoXy6Gk4KzHJdwjeUvY92qzWVbvrVwauDV2vttsoPU7ve9g5eSWKoAUsHr0xJclX0k6RQUVfJIFxUYHUwykmZvFqzO7xqrlRSrqjmKm5e3grFXZCwknWlXFQ50oeromo-9lQUZod_vTTus_WpXXy5m04P792F-Mlb_2Pi08K_AAAA__9CbZH4) in 2025 alone, pledging to partner with Vance's War on Fraud — a powerful midterm message.

* * *

Trump Floats Cuba Takeover

President Trump told reporters Cuba's government is "in a big deal of trouble" and suggested a "[friendly takeover](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOtCAcxJ8GOzcw4OIWFF9jt197pUHA9Z9DMIhe9u0v7iNcN8lkfpn8vp7j01Kk9Ppv12DcSaPPfpwoRhcp1Zz2epSUU13Ckus-guPecrTQY4qjaLxx_i7RBCO0BvDotWoWI0QQylsHdHLuVT-FGZP3YXpIBQ7bkLlIHNAAV1LcIOcewik7Ock7rZjix-ZtDfvN5bSHctpKZ6CU8pVyurm8NtEstW47k_8YBobhukkxXh3DsOVI7s0wUKqhpM_MRoah091DiL51x2TbuVBIPr7bar9DPkNpaznWjWFoivHbD8VI-10zxV-rpQ-7qX9QdRr8BgAA___Yhnml)" could be coming, escalating pressure as the administration cuts off Venezuelan oil shipments to the island.★★★

Sen. Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) is demanding DHS Secretary Kristi Noem [reopen Global Entry](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL1u7CAQhZ8Gd6xg_ANbUNzG3d42pYWHyYKCB8uwXuXtI-cR0h3pSOd8-j4ey8OnnPj532_k8ExLKGFZU86YE7fCtb0OLtwixdLqAgomqUCCWTgvugsOw9RDR04bAwB3a4YuOnvXaCe0Wt9pXIMNFseAuCo1jkrT1CV3LSkAA6CGXt-g_7SgcfAr9mo0gxjUaw--Ub1h4UrH6Vs6KTGXKxW-Ydm67GJrexX9PwGzgPnCTDlfnYA5lo2Y3lXAXIl9IwHzaEY7mF4epRJLLrTJEKus8dVCebN85rL6LInb8S1b9XI_CCPhl4C5O1zY3ynnVCcjBvXcfPr96tof1J0OfgIAAP__U4l_Ig) and stop threatening TSA PreCheck suspensions, accusing the administration of weaponizing travel programs as political leverage during the DHS shutdown.

AI Employees Rally Behind Anthropic

A few weeks ago, Team, the FBI raided the Fulton County, Georgia (home to Atlanta) Elections Operation Center. The Atlanta Journal Constitution (AJC) reported that the activity was “ apparently connected to the Trump administration’s long-held and disproven belief that Fulton’s handling of the 2020 presidential election was rife with fraud .”
You read that right -- instead of focusing on the crucial issues facing our country, MAGA and Trump have weaponized the investigative power of the Justice Department and the FBI to try and justify their lies that the 2020 election was stolen from him .
The search warrant authorized agents to search for and seize all “physical ballots from the 2020 general election” as well as ballot images produced by scanning ballots, voter rolls from that year, and tabulator tapes. It’s highly unlikely the investigation will turn up any vote count fraud connected to the 2020 election results in Fulton County as those results, like elsewhere, have been recounted, audited, and litigated already, costing millions in taxpayer dollars and finding no misdeeds.
That's not stopping the opponents of voting rights in the Trump administration, however. This is their perfect opportunity for a test run of their suppressive power ahead of November's midterm elections.

body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Today, Friday, February 27, is the final day of early voting in Texas for the March primary. Election Day is next Tuesday!
Lizzie has already cast her ballot—and she’s hoping you’ll make a plan to do the same before polls close tonight. If you haven’t voted yet, this is your moment to make your voice heard.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe260227?refcode=lpfe260227 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe260227?refcode=lpfe260227]
Election Day is Tuesday, March 3 , and Democrats across our community are showing up in record numbers! Early turnout has already surpassed what we saw during the entire early voting period in 2022—and we want to keep that momentum going strong through Election Day.
Voters in TX07 can find polling location and hours here:
Harris County voters: http://harrisvotes.com [http://harrisvotes.com]
Fort Bend County voters: http://fortbendcountytx.gov/elections [http://fortbendcountytx.gov/elections]
Every vote matters!
Earlier this week, while President Trump delivered his State of the Union address in Washington, Lizzie chose to spend the evening listening to Houstonians. Instead of attending a speech filled with division and rhetoric, she hosted a community conversation with Houstonians and Texans about what the state of our union really looks like for them.
The stories shared were powerful and urgent. Families are feeling squeezed by rising costs while paychecks struggle to keep up. Housing, groceries, and health care remain out of reach for too many. Community support systems are stretched thin. Long-standing institutions people once relied on aren’t working the way they should—and too many neighbors are living with uncertainty and fear.
But the conversation also revealed something else: resilience. Dedication. A deep commitment to service. From educators and health care workers to local advocates and small business owners, our community is full of people stepping up for one another every day.
Lizzie believes that in moments like this, it’s not speeches that define us—it’s people. It’s neighbors listening to neighbors. It’s communities choosing to move forward together with purpose and patriotism.
Now, it’s time to take the next step.
If you are in Texas and haven’t voted yet, please make your plan today. Let’s keep building a future that reflects the strength, determination, and heart of our community.
Thanks,
Team Lizzie
P.S. Forward this to three people right now to make sure they have a plan to vote!

After wasting weeks of valuable legislative time in December on a ridiculous gerrymandering demand from out-of-state special interests, the Republican majority failed to address a single one of the issues facing our state. All Hoosiers got was more handouts for the rich and higher prices on healthcare and utility bills. While Braun and the Republicans had no problem spending your tax dollars on helipads and luxury vehicles for themselves, they canceled hundreds of road projects across the state and kicked thousands of Hoosiers off their health coverage. ****_Republicans Pass Major Environmental Rollback Bill That Helps Big Polluters_
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126301170/604526522/410550540?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MWQ0YWQ2Ni0yYjE0LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sabk-g5RXDv-UHohvwxJDPf-BUO_HRVHIDpsvQT_fMs=&emci=7163abb9-2114-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=71d4ad66-2b14-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&ceid=4925535) In the last days of the legislative session, Republicans removed IDEM’s legal requirements to sue big polluters by passing SB 277. The GOP supermajority consistently puts polluters over Hoosier health and we are paying the price. In Northwest Indiana, this change could force the Indiana Dunes National Park, our state’s only national park, to close on more days as IDEM will no longer be taking action to keep contamination levels in line with federal standards. SB 277 allows the governor to remove members of the Indiana Environmental Rule Board without cause, and removes the bipartisan membership requirements of the board, politicizing a board which should remain focused on protecting the environment. ****_Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126301171/604526523/1695429573?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MWQ0YWQ2Ni0yYjE0LWYxMTEtYTY5YS0wMDBkM2E1NzU5M2YiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sabk-g5RXDv-UHohvwxJDPf-BUO_HRVHIDpsvQT_fMs=&emci=7163abb9-2114-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&emdi=71d4ad66-2b14-f111-a69a-000d3a57593f&ceid=4925535) Illegal tariffs have Hoosiers paying more for essentials, and families spent over $2,000 extra on goods last year because of Trump’s illegal taxes. In response to the Supreme Court order last week declaring these tariffs illegal, Indiana Democratic legislators made two simple proposals. The first would’ve demanded that the state ask the federal government for a refund from tariff costs, and the second would’ve created a Tariff Mitigation Impact Tax Credit to make sure small businesses can recoup their losses. Maine Gov. Janet Mills (D) learned the hard way Friday that President Donald J. Trump was serious about declaring War on Fraud during his Tuesday State of the Union Address.
Mills, unbeknownst to the rest of Maine, had quietly pleaded with the federal government for extra time to comply with a Feb. 6 demand from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services for detailed records related to Maine's administration of the multi-billion-dollar welfare program known in Maine as MaineCare.
The Trump Administration has rejected Gov. Janet Mills' request for a 30-day extension to turn over records demanded by federal officials examining billing practices in Maine's Medicaid, delivering a blunt message that foot-dragging will not be tolerated in President Donald Trump's recently declared War on Fraud.
In a letter dated Thursday and addressed to Mills and the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) Commissioner Sara Gagne-Holmes, CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz stated that CMS is unable to grant the extension sought by the state on Feb. 19.

"After careful consideration, CMS is unable to grant the requested extension," Oz said, according to a copy of the letter obtained by _The Robinson Report_. "The State's request did not provide sufficient justification or detail regarding the specific challenges preventing timely compliance with CMS's information request."
The original Feb. 6 [letter](https://substack.com/redirect/58020547-83b1-417d-93ab-46933f4c808a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from CMS -- the agency tasked with providing oversight to Maine's largest welfare program, MaineCare -- sent shockwaves through the Mills administration and the state bureaucracy.
That first CMS letter demanded detailed records and answers on MaineCare billing tied to rehabilitative and community support services for children diagnosed with autism.
It's unclear when the Mills administration asked for extra time to comply with the federal oversight request.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/redirect/570d4110-f5a0-46a6-ba87-e68631c4b572?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Oz's Feb. 27 denial letter stressed the urgency of CMS's investigation.
"Meeting the original deadline is necessary to ensure timely federal oversight, avoid delays in program monitoring, and enable CMS to take any actions that may be needed to protect beneficiaries and preserve program integrity," he wrote.
Oz added:
> _" CMS takes the identification, pursuit, and resolution of fraud seriously. Given the magnitude and urgency of the serious program integrity concerns identified in our February 6, 2026, letter, prompt state response is essential to fulfill our shared obligations to protect federal and state taxpayer dollars and ensure beneficiaries receive appropriate services."_
He concluded with a direct warning about the political optics.
"Delaying that important work is not aligned with the Trump Administration's government-wide approach to crushing fraud and sends a signal to taxpayers that both the administration and the State do not take this seriously," Oz said.
The denial comes one month after a federal audit from the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General laid bare systemic documentation failures in MaineCare payments for autism services in 2023. The OIG estimated at least $45.6 million in improper payments that year for rehabilitative and community support services provided to children with autism, with the federal share totaling $28.7 million that auditors are demanding Maine refund immediately.
The audit, issued Jan. 16 and posted publicly Jan. 22, examined a statistically valid sample of claims. Every single one of the 100 "enrollee-months" reviewed contained errors, according to the report.
Eighty-one percent of the sampled months lacked required comprehensive assessments or necessary staff and parent signatures, leaving no valid proof that care was authorized. Nearly two-thirds failed basic documentation requirements, such as supporting the number of units actually billed. In some cases, providers submitted "cloned" session notes -- identical descriptions copied and pasted across different visits -- that showed no unique progress for the child.
Ninety-two percent of the sample included "nontherapy time," with taxpayers billed for lunches, breaks and naps. One out of every five sampled months involved providers who could not prove they held the required licenses or certificates to treat the children.
That's a staggering amount of potential fraud within just one program -- services for children with autism -- for just one year. And that program also happens to be the same Medicaid service area exploited by Somali fraudsters in Minnesota and, allegedly, by Somali-American Abdullahi Ali's [Gateway Community Services](https://substack.com/redirect/e1852978-1245-4a99-9c19-a8ea1c22ca60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) here in Maine.
According to the CMS audit, the problems persisted even as spending on these services exploded from $52.2 million in 2019 to $80.6 million in 2023, a period that coincided with Mills' repeated expansions of MaineCare eligibility.
Mills first action as governor in 2019 was to radically expand Medicaid eligibility to include close to 100,000 new individuals, including able-bodied childless adults. Two years later, Mills worked with Democratic lawmakers to further expand Medicaid eligibility to include a broader class of noncitizens.
The OIG traced the lapses in cost-management observed in the audit to a decade-long oversight vacuum: the state has not conducted a statewide post-payment review of these providers since the child autism program began in 2010.
Notably, the Mills administration hasn't even bothered to rebut the audit's damning findings.
Maine officials "potentially concurred" with the demand to refund the $28.7 million federal share and said they would review the flagged claims and update state rules to address the oversight gaps that persisted for 15 years.
In other words, they admitted that the CMS audit had flagged real lapses in oversight but lacked any basis to respond to the audit -- in part because there's been no oversight of the program.
Oz's Feb. 6 letter set a 30-day deadline -- a deadline the state apparently believes it won't be able to meet.
In a public X post on Feb. 6, Oz referenced Minnesota's Medicaid fraud issues and stated: "Maine also needs to clean up its act." He noted the OIG report identified at least $45 million in improper payments to the state's Medicaid-funded treatment program for children with autism and warned that CMS was ready to act if unsatisfied with Maine's response.
Oz's report is only a small part of a much bigger crisis within Maine's Medicaid program, a program that comprises the largest single spending item in every biannual budget.
The autism billing dispute does not exist in isolation. MaineCare, the state's largest welfare program, faces multiple layers of federal scrutiny.
A congressional investigation led by House Oversight Committee Chairman Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) is examining whether Mills administration officials improperly used federal Medicaid funds to cover benefits for noncitizens, including those without lawful immigration status. The Oct. 3, 2025, inquiry targeted Maine and seven other states that provide some Medicaid benefits to noncitizens using state funds and asked whether costs were improperly shifted to federal reimbursement. _The Robinson Report_ submitted a Freedom of Access Act request for DHHS records on the state's response; DHHS acknowledged receipt but has not provided a timeline or cost estimate as required by state law.
As detailed extensively at _The Maine Wire_ and by _The Robinson Report_ , Medicaid payment data obtained through a Freedom of Access Act request, and federal provider payment data released this month by the federal Department of Health and Human Services, have revealed explosive growth in spending on high-risk health care sectors like "personal care services."
The data have also revealed that Maine's most suspect Medicaid providers are charging, 3x, 4x, and even 5x the national average for the exact same services. As another example, federal Medicaid data shows Maine is paying roughly $120 per claim for Methadone/Suboxone treatments while providers in the rest of the country receive just $20 per claim.
The Medicaid spending data also shows improbably rapid growth in billing among hundreds of MaineCare agencies that have popped into existence since 2020, including home health agencies that are suspiciously clustered at identical addresses where they maintain "ghost suites" -- aka single room offices that are almost always vacant.
The federal investigation and the congressional probe further certify reporting from _The Maine Wire_ and _The Robinson Report_ , which last year exposed more than $1.6 million in improper payments to Gateway Community Services. _The Robinson Report_ was also the first outlet to raise the testimony of former Gateway employee Christopher Bernardini, a billing specialist who laid out in detail how Gateway supervisors systemically defrauded Medicaid at the direction of CEO Abdullahi Ali.
Ali has since fled to Africa where he's believed to be living on an estate he purchased shortly after receiving nearly $700,000 under the PPP loan program.
Subscribe to the only news publication in Maine that doesn't get no-bid contracts from Janet Mills...
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..BAKpsvnyAD03hijaEbBPS1adCFVfgsVDuIBdWGG7GFM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=189400252)
Yet Gateway is far from the only Medicaid/MaineCare firm that's raised eyebrows with sky-high billing figures and no obvious services.
At 75 Bishop St. in Portland, multiple home health agencies operate from the same address, including 5 Stars Home Health Care. A DHHS audit found that agency over-billed MaineCare by nearly $400,000 after failing to produce required documentation despite multiple extensions. The agency's sign remained on the door when reporters visited in January 2026. By Feb. 2025, DHHS stopped payments to 25-year-old CEO Mostafa Alahmedi, but there's no indication he was investigated criminally after walking away from the Medicaid program with more than one million dollars.

Frey's paranoid attempt to block contact with Justice Department officials and Gagne-Holmes's ham-handed subpoena email combine to paint a portrait of a state bureaucracy deathly afraid of the transparency that would result when investigators who cannot be controlled or intimidated by the Mills Administration gain access to state records.
But the multiple federal investigations into Maine's multi-billion dollar welfare program could have far more severe consequences for the state than exposing corruption or embarrassing Democrat loyalists. The dispute between Washington, D.C., and Augusta over Maine's program could have far-reaching consequences for the state's financial future.
Medicaid is jointly funded by the state and federal governments, with the federal government picking up the larger share of the cost, especially in states that expanded Medicaid eligibility pursuant to the Affordable Care Act, aka ObamaCare. Because the Feds pay the bills, they also get to set the rules. One of those rules is that states like Maine that provided Medicaid benefits to noncitizens may not reimburse themselves from the federal coffers, i.e. the Feds refuse to pay for noncitizen welfare.
Because Maine offers abundant welfare benefits to noncitizens, including Medicaid benefits, the state must differentiate between noncitizen welfare payments and citizen welfare payments, because only citizen welfare payments can be offloaded onto the Feds. If, however, the Mills administration tried to make Maine's stretched budget work by shifting non-citizen welfare costs onto the federal government, Maine could be on the hook for hundreds of millions of dollars in illegal reimbursements.
That's just one example of Medicaid money the Trump administration could clawback from Maine if a deeper investigation finds that the Mills administration skirted federal rules for administering the welfare program.
The autism audit alone threatens a significant fiscal hit. Maine must repay the $28.7 million federal share immediately, while another $22.4 million ($14.2 million federal) was flagged as potentially improper due to unverifiable documentation. With the legislative session underway, the Mills administration and Democratic lawmakers face a fiscal straitjacket as they confront not only the refund demand but the broader implications for program integrity.
Considering that Medicaid spending typically comprises 25% to 30% of every biennial budget, a moderate clawback from the federal government could send state government reeling.
If Mills is feeling the pressure of a potential budget crisis caused by increased federal scrutiny, she did not show any signs of it in her recent State of the State speech, which the candidate for the Democratic U.S. Senate nomination used primarily as an opportunity to pose for her campaign videographers.
In her speech, Mills said she would repeat her 2022 pre-election ploy of sending $300 checks to potential voters just prior to the election.
Depending on how the CMS audit goes, Maine's "Rainy Day Fund," the pool of money Mills intends to raid for her vote-buying payouts, may get sucked back into Washington, D.C., to repay the Feds for Mills' mismanaged Medicaid program.
Oz's letter closes insisting on expeditious compliance.
"CMS values its partnership with the State of Maine in meeting federal oversight requirements and ensuring the receipt of high quality, timely information," he said. "We look forward to receiving your complete response within 30 days from the receipt of our February 6, 2026, letter."
That would give the Mills admin ten days to comply -- but six days if we're counting days when government employees are actually at their desks.

subject: Donald Trump isn’t the disease. He’s one of its worst symptoms.

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=1771%2E251025%2Ew0awli ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=1771%2E251025%2Ew0awli ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter, there’s something that keeps happening at our town halls.

At nearly every event, a few people come in a little late and usually sit
in the back. You can tell they’re curious, but not fully bought in.

After speaking to the general room, I usually try to find those folks and
ask why they came.

I’ve heard some version of the same answer multiple times now:

“I don’t really believe that any politician does what they say they’re
going to do. I don’t think anyone has real solutions for me. But my
friends were excited about you, so I figured I’d see for myself.”

That honesty doesn’t offend me — it’s the truth about this moment we’re
in.

There’s an overwhelming sense of pessimism regarding politics, especially
among young people. Built-up frustration around the broken systems that
impact our daily lives, like healthcare, and a feeling that no matter
who’s in power, nothing ever really changes.

These feelings didn’t come out of nowhere,
Peter.

For decades, corporate PACs, billionaires, and super PACs have shaped our
politics. They fund an overwhelming share of campaigns, and too often,
they decide what gets prioritized in Washington, not the voters.

That’s the disease I’ve been calling out for years. Donald Trump isn’t the
disease. He’s one of its worst symptoms.

So, back to those town hall conversations. Here’s what I tell them:

We may not solve every problem overnight. The question of our lives is
whether we tried.

We’re trying to build something here that takes on the status quo and
fights to build something better: A campaign that refuses corporate PAC
and AIPAC money, and speaks clearly about healthcare, civil liberties, and
an economy that works for working people.

But if we’re going to challenge the well-funded forces that have clung to
power for decades, we need the resources to compete with them.

That’s why I’m turning to you,
Peter. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260227-2-ak.NpvHgc&amount=10&refcode=em20260227-1766&t=1004&akid=1771%2E251025%2Ew0awli ]If you believe in
building something better, will you chip in $10 or whatever
you can to fuel our campaign?

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

name: David Hogg
subject: Stephen Lynch thinks he owns his seat
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Stephen Lynch doesn’t think he owes his constituents anything but excuses. Patrick Roath knows Massachusetts deserves more.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260227-1&t=1&akid=3194%2E587540%2EM4SMEA)
Peter,
Earlier this month at a rally, a frustrated constituent called out Rep. Stephen Lynch for not doing enough to fight back against Trump’s abuses of power and protect our democracy.
Instead of hearing them out, his response was to dismiss their comment completely, telling the very people he’s supposed to serve that what he does is _his_ decision to make, and if they don’t like it, they can run for Congress themselves. After two decades in office, this is how he acts.
**This is the problem with Democrats, Peter.**
There’s a sense of entitlement that’s taken root. A belief that once the election is won and you’re “safe” in your seat, listening to your constituents is optional. That instead of demanding better, voters should fall in line with the options they’ve been given.
That’s not how democracy works, and it’s certainly not how you win elections.
**When our leaders act like they own their seats instead of working everyday to earn them, people start to lose faith in our party and our democracy — and justifiably so.**
But we aren’t going to settle for that. We won’t be cornered into supporting candidates that don’t want to hear from us, and won’t prioritize the issues that matter to us most.
Like Lynch said: if you want a say, run for Congress. We’ll gladly take him up on that offer.
**Leaders We Deserve is backing Patrick Roath,** a bold young leader who has consistently stepped up to serve his community when it matters most, and delivered real results for the people of Massachusetts. He’s fought to protect voting rights, asylum seekers, and has stood up for working families time and time again.
Patrick’s priorities won’t be firing back at his own constituents or taking a lukewarm approach to Trump’s attacks on our freedom. They’ll be to make affordable housing a reality, address the high costs of childcare, and to put forth an agenda that’s driven by working people and the issues that they face.
And Patrick’s campaign is powered entirely by grassroots supporters. No corporate cash, and no billionaire donors. That means he’s counting on people like you to help him compete against a 20+ year incumbent armed with establishment support and deep-pocketed donors.
**[If you believe elected officials have a duty to respond to the needs of their constituents, pitch in $5 today to make sure Patrick has the resources he needs to beat Lynch in September.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260227_1_patrick.peHBcV&refcode=em20260227-3194&amount=5&t=2&akid=3194%2E587540%2EM4SMEA)**

Thank you for being a part of this movement with us.
With gratitude,
David Hogg

I met longtime activists, first-time delegates, young families, veterans, and patriots who understand what’s at stake in 2026.But conventions are just the beginning.If we’re going to turn that enthusiasm into victory, we need to:
---
* Equip and activate grassroots delegates
* Expand our county-level organization
* Fund volunteer recruitment and training
* Strengthen turnout operations across MN-01

---
The Left is already organizing. National Democrats are watching our district closely. We cannot afford to coast. Most Mississippians agree on this: every child's life is precious, and every preventable infant death is a tragedy. But good intentions are not a blank check for government power. With House Bill 1637, the Mississippi Legislature is quietly asking us to trade away privacy and transparency in the name of "review."
HB 1637 would create a new Fetal and Infant Mortality Review Panel inside state government. On the surface, that sounds reasonable. Who wouldn't want to understand why babies die and how to prevent it?
The trouble lies in how this panel would operate. The bill gives it sweeping authority to dig into deeply personal medical information and government records, while shielding its own work from public view.
In plain English, here's what HB 1637 does:
* Creates a state panel with broad power to obtain confidential medical records and data from hospitals, clinics, and multiple state and local agencies.
* Allows the panel to compel agencies to hand over information, backed by state enforcement power.
* Exempts the panel's meetings and records from Mississippi's Open Meetings Act and Public Records Act, meaning citizens and the press are locked out.

That combination should alarm anyone who cares about civil liberties, whether you lean left, right, or somewhere in between.
Imagine you're a young mother who suffered a heartbreaking stillbirth or lost a newborn in the NICU. Under HB 1637, a government panel could access your medical records, related agency files, and sensitive information about your family. You might never know who saw it, what they concluded, or how it might be used--because the panel's work would be hidden behind closed doors.
Or imagine a rural doctor already struggling to keep a small practice afloat. The panel could demand extensive records and data, with little recourse if the doctor believes the request is overbroad or intrusive. Complying takes time, money, and staff--resources pulled away from patient care, under threat of state enforcement.
Supporters say confidentiality is necessary to encourage honest review. But Mississippi already has laws that protect patient privacy and shield certain quality-improvement processes, while still respecting open meetings and public records requirements. HB 1637 goes much further: it builds a black box inside government, fueled by our most private information and answerable to almost no one.
When government gains the power to see more, the people should gain the power to see more, too. This bill flips that principle on its head. It expands state access and coercive authority while shrinking public oversight.
If we truly want to reduce infant mortality, we should invest in proven, transparent solutions: better prenatal care, community health outreach, support for high-risk mothers, and data sharing governed by clear privacy safeguards and public accountability--not a secretive panel armed with your medical records.
Mississippi can pursue compassionate, evidence-based policies without undermining core civil liberties. Legislators should reject HB 1637 or, at minimum, go back to the drawing board with strict limits on data access, strong privacy protections, and full transparency to the people.
Contact your state representative and senator today. Tell them you support protecting babies--and you also support protecting privacy and open government. Ask them to vote NO on HB 1637.

# Hegseth forces Scouts back to basics - No more DEI!
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced Friday that the Pentagon will maintain support for Scouting America after the group agreed to eliminate all DEI programs, recognize only biological sex at birth for membership, **[ban shared intimate spaces by boys and girls,](https://substack.com/redirect/6eada0c7-8396-4589-b09e-5f99084993b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and refocus on developing boys into men, averting a threatened cutoff of military access and aid.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6eada0c7-8396-4589-b09e-5f99084993b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **DEI Purge Confirmed** -- Scouting America commits to removing all diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives, including divisive language from programs and publications, with "No more DEI. Zero."
* **Merit Badge Overhaul** -- The organization will discontinue the "Citizenship in Society" badge promoting DEI concepts required for Eagle Scout advancement.
* **Biological Sex Policy** -- Membership forms will list only "male" and "female" based on birth sex, prohibiting biological boys and girls from sharing tents, showers, or toilets.
* **Military Partnership Preserved** -- Under a signed MOU, Scouting America retains access to Department of War facilities and logistical support, with Hegseth planning reviews to ensure compliance and a return to traditional boy-focused scouting.

# **CNN staffers panic as Paramount Skydance acquires Warner Bros. Discovery, plans centrist shift**
CNN staffers **[are"apoplectic" and "freaking out"](https://substack.com/redirect/8d3be5e3-63f1-412d-aaa7-570a07e239a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after learning that left-leaning network owner Warner Bros. Discovery will be acquired by Paramount Skydance for $80.5 billion, with insiders confirming the new owners plan a more politically centrist approach to news. Paramount Skydance scooped up CBS last year and tapped 41-year-old journalist Bari Weiss to root out liberal bias at that network.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8d3be5e3-63f1-412d-aaa7-570a07e239a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** CNN President Mark Thompson was forced to send a memo late Thursday to tamp down anxiety, writing "don't jump to conclusions about the future until we know more." Staffers believe President Trump will be "on the phone daily orchestrating coverage" with the Ellisons (PSKY is run by indie producer David Ellison and financed by his father, longtime Trump supporter and Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison) and Weiss, though one PSKY insider told The Post "we're looking to produce a news product that appeals to 70% of the country that is either center left or center right."
* **What 's next:** The bigger concern for CNN talent from Kaitlan Collins, Jake Tapper and Anderson Cooper down to rank-and-file staff is likely cost cutting, though CNN still makes money with $600 million in projected adjusted operating profit on $1.8 billion revenue this year. PSKY plans to merge CNN with its CBS news division (which Weiss runs), meaning some top producers and anchors could be axed, and questions remain about whether Thompson will stay given Weiss's presence. The merger still requires approval from Trump's Department of Justice and other regulators.

Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodriguez Thursday, urging him to end US sanctions and the oil blockade in a dramatic shift toward cooperation following the US-backed ouster of Nicolas Maduro in January. If things don’t pick up, that means we need to take a serious look at budget cuts. And in a district as competitive as this one, that’s the last thing we want to be doing.

**The bottom line: The only way we’ll be able to raise the funds to run a competitive campaign is with your help.** ****

clean_body: An important deadline approaches | | Matt Maasdam is a husband, a father, and a Navy SEAL. He carried the nuclear football for President Obama — now he's running as a Democrat to flip Michigan's 7th congressional district. If you’d like to unsubscribe, | | Hey, it’s Emma — Matt’s campaign manager in MI-07. Tomorrow, we have to close the books on this end-of-month fundraising deadline. To tell you the truth: ever since Cook Political Report listed us as the tipping point for control of the House, Republicans have doubled down on their spending here. We must close the gap tonight. Otherwise, we’re in serious danger of not hitting our fundraising marks for the month. But if you need to hear a little more, I’ve prepared this memo to give you a full picture.** | TO: Interested Parties FROM: Matt Maasdam for Congress MEMO: Fundraising in MI-07 MI-07 is now recognized as the path to taking back the House. It’s one of the most competitive battleground districts in the country, changing parties after every election in recent years. Our opponent, Tom Barrett, is beatable. This is a winnable district. But we need to be ready for a tough fight. National Republicans have already heavily invested in this district — Mike Johnson and corporations have given hundreds of thousands to my opponent. We’re going to be in for a tough fight. But Matt is exactly the candidate for the job. About Matt: Matt Maasdam is a Navy SEAL who served under Presidents of both parties in Iraq, Afghanistan, and at the White House. Over 20 years in the Navy, he served in some of the world’s most dangerous and complex environments. As President Obama’s Military Aide, he carried the nuclear football. He’s spent his entire career protecting this country, and fighting for accountability, and practicing the values of integrity and service. He has what it takes to beat Barrett and flip this district. Where you come in: Our team has set some ambitious fundraising goals to meet this month. We based these goals based on our performance from January — but we simply aren’t receiving as many donations this month as we were last month. If things don’t pick up, that means we need to take a serious look at budget cuts. And in a district as competitive as this one, that’s the last thing we want to be doing. The bottom line: The only way we’ll be able to raise the funds to run a competitive campaign is with your help. If we want to take back the House, we need to crush this deadline — and the one after it, and the one after that. Please. I wouldn’t be emailing if it wasn’t important. Two senators from opposing parties are pushing the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to renew and expand a health care screening program aimed at uninsured and underinsured women.

Sens. Angela Alsobrooks and Katie Britt introduced the new legislation on Thursday. It would expand access to a CDC program that provides heart health risk screenings and other medical support. The bill authorizes $250 million over the next five years to increase eligibility for the program and permit additional health care providers to participate.

MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WSFA) - Republican Alabama Sen. Katie Britt has co-sponsored a new bill in Congress with Democratic Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand to protect elderly individuals from financial fraud.

The legislation, called the Guarding Unprotected Aging Retirees from Deception, or GUARD Act, aims to bring online scammers to justice. The bill allows local police departments to allocate certain grant funding towards investigating financial fraud through blockchain technology, which can create a permanent, transparent record of transactions and help law enforcement track stolen funds.

body:

Peter, _**We have exciting news to share.**_ Chaz’s campaign has been officially named to the DCCC’s Red to Blue program. This designation is competitive and selective. body:
Donald Trump came to Georgia.

The White House sent him here to do damage control on tariffs and health care.

But he just couldn’t help himself: instead of trying to defend his price-inflating tariffs and insurance-premium-doubling health care policy, he resorted to repeating conspiracy theories about the 2020 election — an election he lost in Georgia despite pressuring Georgia election officials to “find” him more votes.

Maybe he’s been watching the rallies I’ve been holding across Georgia, where thousands have turned out in opposition to his corruption and depravity. Because he took a moment to throw some insults my way.

Now, Donald Trump has been insulting me for a long time. But this time, it didn’t seem like his heart was in it. I think you could see in his eyes and hear in his voice that he knows he’s lost the American people. That he knows his Presidency is slipping away. That he can feel Georgians, and people nationwide, preparing to deliver a decisive rebuke of historic abuses of power.

Because as I travel across Georgia, what I hear is more and more people of every background and belief reject Trump’s chaos and corruption. And it's not just Democrats and independents. It’s Republicans too!

More and more Republicans take me aside, or they call me on the phone. They tell me they don’t like where this President has taken us. And they tell me they’re going to support a Democrat for the first time.

But here’s the thing: as he gets more desperate, his abuses become more dangerous. From sending Tulsi Gabbard on ballot raids in Fulton County, Georgia, to threatening a national takeover of elections, we have to be ready for anything.

We have to turn out LANDSLIDE margins of victory ... victories so decisive that no scheme or plot hatched in the White House can foil the will of the people.

And we have to defend voting rights with unprecedented tenacity and resources.

**I need your help to do these things.**

Because he took a moment to throw some insults my way. Now, Donald Trump has been insulting me for a long time. But this time, it didn’t seem like his heart was in it. I think you could see in his eyes and hear in his voice that he knows he’s lost the American people. That he knows his Presidency is slipping away. That he can feel Georgians, and people nationwide, preparing to deliver a decisive rebuke of historic abuses of power. Because as I travel across Georgia, what I hear is more and more people of every background and belief reject Trump’s chaos and corruption. And it's not just Democrats and independents. It’s Republicans too! More and more Republicans take me aside, or they call me on the phone. They tell me they don’t like where this President has taken us. And they tell me they’re going to support a Democrat for the first time. But here’s the thing: as he gets more desperate, his abuses become more dangerous. Chuck is back from Oaxaca. Mike is slightly less angry than last week. And the 2026 midterms just got a whole lot more interesting.
In the latest episode of The Latino Vote Podcast, _**" The 2026 Latino Vote Battlefield"**_, dives headfirst into the districts, demographics, and power struggles that will decide control of Congress. And at the center of it all?

**Latino voters.** Not as a side story. Not as an afterthought. But as the battlefield itself.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/9cf74263-793d-4b34-aa6f-a84a88ee388f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c512b08d-e1d3-4f9a-b6df-5c1e44373eb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
